summary: Aaron Hadlow's freestyle legacy reborn. PRoWELD LE, Flight_X canopy for a softer controlled feel, Mylar struts. Only 3 sizes (9, 11, 13m). Designed as a complete system with the dedicated Hadlow Pro bar and Descent board. Built to revive and push freestyle performance forward.
best_for: Dedicated freestyle and unhooked trick riders

sources.summary: Aaron Hadlow's passion project and it's the real deal. The Flight_X canopy gives a distinctly different feel to the Thrive — more precise slack and pop for unhooked moves. Very niche but excellent.
If you care about freestyle, this is the most interesting new C-style kite in years. Aaron Hadlow built what he wanted and riders who've tried it are impressed.

reviews.summary: Gleiten tv tested the 11m and 13m Hadlow Pro in challenging 10–30 knot gusty, rainy conditions alongside the matching Descent board. They highlighted the welded leading edge construction, exceptional gust stability, and perfectly tuned bar feel for unhooked freestyle, drawing comparisons to the Duotone Vegas while noting the Hadlow Pro's more damped and controlled power delivery as a meaningful step forward. Peak pop versus top competitors remained unconfirmed due to the difficult test conditions.

structured_review.summary: The Harlem Hadlow Pro 2025 is a focused five-strut freestyle kite built on Aaron Hadlow's legacy, delivering exceptional bar feel, precise slack, and damped power delivery that suits both unhooked freestyle and hooked-in performance. Its welded PRoWELD construction and Flight_X canopy produce a stability and gust resistance unusual for a dedicated freestyle kite. The caveat is its narrow three-size range and the fact that peak pop performance in perfect conditions wasn't fully testable by the reviewer.
pros: Exceptionally tuned bar feel for unhooked freestyle — responsive but optimally positioned
Welded leading edge and canopy construction delivers outstanding flight stability and gust resistance up to 30 knots
Smooth, strong but never abrupt power delivery with no dead-spot tendency
Wide effective wind range for a five-strut freestyle kite
Easy relaunch — critical for freestyle use when crashes are routine
Hooked-in jump performance rivals three-strut freeride kites when the kite is actively moved
cons: Only available in three sizes (9, 11, 13m), limiting precise size matching
Peak unhooked pop versus proven competitors could not be confirmed due to poor test conditions
Hangtime on hooked jumps is inherently lower than dedicated freeride/big-air kites
Full performance potential requires pairing with the dedicated Descent board and Hadlow Pro bar
structured_review.best_for: Freestyle and wakestyle riders who want a refined, stable, and controllable unhooked kite with legitimate freeride crossover capability.
structured_review.not_for: Riders focused primarily on big air, hangtime, or who need more than three size options to fine-tune their quiver.
structured_review.rec_blurb: Aaron Hadlow's freestyle DNA, now with damped control that forgives bad conditions.
